comments.content: The DELETE handler performs the same authorization/activity lookup as PATCH but with no linkage check, so any authorized user can delete an agenda item belonging to another activity by supplying their own `id`. Scope the delete to the activity, e.g. `await prisma.activityAgendaItem.deleteMany({ where: { id: params.agendaId, activityId: params.id } })` and return 404 when nothing was deleted. Also consider extracting the shared auth+ownership lookup into a helper to remove the duplication between PATCH and DELETE.

GET has no authentication/authorization check, unlike POST. Any unauthenticated caller can enumerate agenda items (including moderator/speaker names, organizations and avatars) for arbitrary activity ids. It also doesn't verify the activity exists, so invalid ids silently return an empty list instead of 404. Add a `requireAuthenticatedUser`/`requireRoleAccess` check and return 404 when the activity is missing.

`requireRoleAccess` takes a `Locale` and `UserRole[]`; passing `"en" as any` defeats type checking (and violates the no-`any` rule) while the role array uses bare strings. If `UserRole` is derived from an enum/union, a typo here would silently bypass or break auth. Use the typed locale and role constants (e.g. `UserRole.ADMIN`, `UserRole.EVENT_MANAGER`) without the cast.

comments.content: The agenda item is created and then the speaker links are created in a separate call with no transaction. If the second call fails, the item persists without speakers (partial write); concurrently the returned `item` never includes the just-created speakers. Also, `data.speakerIds` are inserted without verifying the speakers exist or belong to this activity, so invalid/FK-orphan ids can be linked. Use `prisma.$transaction` and validate/scope the speaker ids (e.g. `speaker: { activityId: params.id }` filter) before linking.

`agendaDate` is regex-validated as `YYYY-MM-DD` but then passed to `new Date(...)`, which interprets it as UTC midnight. A `YYYY-MM-DD` string like `2026-13-45` passes the regex but produces `Invalid Date`, which will fail on write; and storing UTC midnight can shift the displayed day for non-UTC viewers. Validate the parsed date (reject `Invalid Date`) and store a consistent date representation (date-only or explicit timezone). Similarly, `startTime`/`endTime` are stored raw with no check that `endTime > startTime`, which can corrupt the ordering/sorting semantics.

comments.content: Rate limiting only keys on the user subject, so a moderator writing rapid comments is equally throttled; more importantly the check happens before body parsing, meaning invalid-payload requests (400) still consume the user's comment quota. Consider validating the body first and then applying the rate limit so legitimate retries after a validation error are not penalized.

All three access checks (community existence, participant, mode) are performed before the rate limit, so unauthenticated-ish/unprivileged callers can trigger repeated DB lookups without throttling. Also, the 400 error message states "Plain text without personal contact information is required", which conflates empty/invalid input with the contact-info rejection rule and is not actionable for the client. Returning distinct messages would make debugging and UX clearer.

comments.content: Missing authorization and validation on the GET handler: any unauthenticated caller can read the type-specific config of any activity id, and there is no `canManageActivity`/role check like the PATCH handler has. Since this config can contain sensitive draft configuration, apply the same authorization (or an explicit public-read allowlist) before returning the detail.

GET returns 200 with `detail: null` for a non-existent activity, which masks invalid ids and makes client-side error handling ambiguous. Check that the activity exists and return 404 when it does not.

Prisma calls are not wrapped in try/catch, so DB/constraint failures surface as unhandled 500s without a controlled error payload. Wrap the queries (and this upsert) so failures return a structured 500 response.

`configJson` is only checked to be a non-null object: arrays pass `typeof === "object"`, and there is no size or schema validation before persisting arbitrary user-controlled JSON. Reject arrays, enforce a max payload size, and validate against the expected config shape to prevent storing arbitrary/unbounded data.

comments.content: Authorization is applied before checking the activity type: any ADMIN/EVENT_MANAGER can export applications of a `PROJECT` activity. The sibling list endpoint (`app/api/activities/[id]/applications/route.ts`) explicitly routes PROJECT activities through `canReviewProjectApplication(...)` instead of the role-based manager check, so this export route is inconsistent and likely leaks project applicant PII to users who are not project reviewers. Align the PROJECT branch with the list endpoint (use the project-specific permission check) and only fall back to `canManageActivity` for non-project activities.

`findMany` has no `take`/pagination limit, so an activity with a very large applicant pool will load every application (plus joined user/consent rows) into memory and build the whole CSV string in memory, which can exhaust server memory or hit the execution time limit. Add a bounded `take` (or stream the export in batches) and handle the truncated case.

comments.content: Both handlers are declared `async` but never `await` anything and can never reject, so the `async` keyword is dead/unnecessary. Drop it to make it clear no error handling is required here.

`requireRoleAccess` uses `redirect()` on authentication/authorization failure (see lib/server/auth.ts:186-194). Next's `redirect()` works by throwing a `NEXT_REDIRECT` error. In this API route, `requireRoleAccess` is called WITHOUT a try/catch and outside any Next.js page/route handling that would translate that redirect into a 3xx response. For API routes, the thrown redirect error is not handled, so an unauthenticated or unauthorized request will surface as an unhandled error / 500 instead of a proper 401/403. Additionally, since `roles` already includes ADMIN/EVENT_MANAGER here, the role check provides no in-handler authorization failure path. Handle the thrown redirect (or use `getCurrentUser` + explicit 401/403 JSON responses) so API clients get correct status codes.

None of the GET/POST/DELETE handlers wrap the `requireRoleAccess`, `canManageActivityVerifiers`, or Prisma calls in try/catch. A transient DB error, Prisma validation error (e.g. malformed `params.id`/`userId`), or the thrown `redirect` error from auth will escape as an unhandled rejection and produce a 500 with no user-facing error message, violating the async error-handling standard. Wrap the handler bodies in try/catch and return a controlled JSON error (e.g. 500) instead.

TOCTOU race between the `findUnique` existence check and `create`. Two concurrent POSTs for the same `(userId, activityId)` can both pass the check; the second `create` then violates the `@@unique([userId, activityId])` (P2002) constraint and throws an unhandled error (500) instead of the intended 409. Prefer creating directly and catching the unique-constraint error (P2002 -> 409), or use an upsert-style/`createMany` with `skipDuplicates` approach.

Same TOCTOU pattern in DELETE: between `findUnique` and `delete`, a concurrent request can delete the record, causing `delete` to throw P2025 (record not found) as an unhandled 500. Use `deleteMany({ where: { userId, activityId } })` and inspect `count`, or catch P2025.

`requireRoleAccess("en" as any, ...)` uses a double cast (`"en" as any`) that defeats the `Locale` type; the locale is hardcoded to "en" rather than derived from the request, so localized sign-in/redirect behavior is lost on these API endpoints. Consider typing the locale param properly and deriving it (or documenting why "en" is fixed) instead of bypassing the type system with `as any`.

The `findUnique` -> `create` is a non-atomic check, but more importantly the POST flows expose whether an activity exists/ownership via distinct 404 'Activity not found' responses. Combined with no validation of `params.id`/`userId` format, malformed IDs can leak differing Prisma errors. Consider validating `id`/`userId` (e.g. UUID format) and returning a generic error to avoid information disclosure and unexpected Prisma errors.

comments.content: Audit logging and both notification creates swallow all errors via `.catch(() => undefined)`. In this withdrawal flow, a silently failed audit write leaves a gap in the security trail, and a failed notification means the counterparty is never informed while the API still returns success. At minimum log the failure through the project logger; consider surfacing a non-fatal warning in the response.

The withdraw flow and the review-update flow both re-fetch the user and re-run authorization with duplicated branches. Since `requireRoleAccess` is invoked after the DB read and its result is checked with `instanceof NextResponse`, note that this helper actually throws a redirect rather than returning a `NextResponse` (see `lib/server/auth.ts`), so the `adminCheck instanceof NextResponse` guard is dead code and the intended 403 is unreachable. Verify the contract of `requireRoleAccess` and remove the unreachable check.

The legacy (no `occurrenceId`) branch approves an application by directly calling `prisma.activityApplication.update` without any seat accounting. For activities that are occurrence-based this bypasses `admitApplicationToOccurrence`, so no seat is claimed in `activityOccurrence.admittedCount` and a participation is created while the occurrence may already be full. This makes the occurrence capacity invariant bypassable by simply omitting `occurrenceId` from the request. Please require `occurrenceId` (or validate that the activity/application has no occurrence) before taking the non-atomic path.

Read-then-create on `activityParticipation` runs outside any transaction. Under concurrent approvals two requests can both observe `null` and both attempt `create`, producing a P2002 unique-constraint error that is not caught here and will surface as an unhandled 500. Wrap the existence check + create in a transaction or catch the unique-constraint error (as `ensureParticipation` does in activity-occurrences.ts).

`requireRoleAccess` is declared as `(locale: Locale, roles: UserRole[], nextPath?)`. Passing `"en" as any` defeats type-safety (the checklist forbids `any` without justification) and hardcodes the locale. Prefer deriving the locale from the request (e.g. from `getCurrentUser()`/headers) or using a named `Locale` constant instead of an `any` cast.

comments.content: The status update persists `status` unconditionally rather than as an atomic compare-and-set on the previously validated `existing.status`. Two concurrent PATCH requests can both read the same pre-completion `existing.status` and pass the `canTransitionActivityParticipation` check, after which both run `triggerActivityRewards`/`syncParticipationToPassport`. Depending on the reward type this can double-dispatch rewards (e.g. the BADGE path only guards on a `findFirst` + `create` without a unique constraint, so a race can create duplicate awards). Use a conditional update (e.g. `updateMany({ where: { id, status: existing.status }, data: { status } })` and treat `count === 0` as a 409) to make the transition atomic.

Note this also means the delete can succeed while the audit write fails, leaving a destructive action with no audit trail — wrap everything in try/catch and log the error (matching `revoke/route.ts`).

The verification code is copied into the audit metadata. Even though deletable records are expected to have `verificationCode === null`, persisting a public verification identifier in audit storage is unnecessary exposure and contradicts the guard above. The guard already ensures it is null, so drop it from the metadata (keep only `previousStatus`).

The deletable-state rule is inlined here while other lifecycle predicates live in `@/lib/server/certificates` (`canRevokeCertificateStatus`, `canRestoreCertificateStatus`, ...). Duplicating the `DRAFT`/`NONE` rule makes it drift-prone; extract a shared `canDeleteCertificateIssue(issue)` helper and reuse it (also required for the transactional re-check suggested above).

`processCertificateBatchChunk` is awaited without any try/catch. The helper performs many DB round-trips and external certificate issuance which can throw; any thrown error here escapes the handler and results in an unhandled 500 with an internal stack trace, contradicting the intended friendly `{ error }` responses. Wrap the call and return a 500/503 JSON response (also consider logging the error server-side).

Every non-ok result is mapped to 404 with the message "Batch not found.", but `processCertificateBatchChunk` also returns `ok: false` for other failure reasons (e.g. status 400/500 from `writeBatchAudit` audit-log failures). Returning 404 for those misclassifies server-side errors and misleads the admin client into thinking the batch does not exist. Map the status based on the failure reason (e.g. propagate a status/`notFound` flag) instead of hardcoding 404.

Unguarded `await request.json()` on an admin endpoint: an arbitrarily large body is fully buffered and parsed before validation. Since `limit` is an optional scalar, the body can be empty/absent, so pass a default and parse defensively (the JSON syntax itself cannot be expressed in zod). Also consider attaching `schema.safeParse`/a body size guard so oversized payloads do not consume memory. `params.id` is likewise forwarded to Prisma without any format validation — a non-UUID string reaches the DB layer; validate it (e.g. `z.string().uuid()` or the project's id schema) and return 400 before touching the database.

  const payload = retrySchema.safeParse(body ?? {});

TOCTOU on the immutable-key check: `findUnique` → compare → `update` is not atomic, so a concurrent key change between the read and the write can bypass the immutability rule. Wrap the read+write in a single `prisma.$transaction` and compare the key inside the transaction, or enforce it with a DB-level guard.

`requireRoleAccess` is a **server-component/route helper**: it takes a `Locale`, has no `NextRequest`, and resolves the current user from the request-scoped session cookie via `getCurrentUser()`. It cannot serve as a guard for a route handler, and it does not return a `NextResponse`. `"en" as any` also bypasses `Locale` type checking for no reason.

Two concrete problems on this line alone, both affecting all four handlers:
1. `auth instanceof NextResponse return auth` is unreachable — the helper returns `Promise<AuthenticatedUser>` (`getCurrentUser()` → `getCurrentSession()` → `prisma.session.findUnique`). On auth failure it does NOT return 401/403: it calls Next's `redirect()` (throws `NEXT_REDIRECT`), and if no session exists it falls through and returns `undefined`. So a failed cookie decryption throws out of the handler, and an anonymous caller gets `undefined` → `auth instanceof NextResponse` is `false` → execution continues into `prisma.projectMilestone.findMany` as an unauthenticated request. That is an auth bypass for this endpoint (no middleware exists in `apps/passport-web/middleware.ts` to cover it either).
2. Even when it does work, `auth` is never used, so there is no check that the session user has been granted access to the referenced `activityId` (see POST/PATCH/DELETE below) — any globally-privileged role can read/mutate any activity's milestones.

Use a genuine API guard (returning a 401/403 `NextResponse`) plus an activity-level access check, and drop the `as any` cast.

None of the Prisma calls in this file are wrapped in try/catch, so a driver/database failure (or an invalid DATABASE_URL that passes the truthiness check but fails on first query) produces an unhandled rejection and a raw 500 with a stack trace instead of a controlled error response. Wrap each handler body in try/catch and return a sanitized 500 (log the real error server-side).

comments.content: The legacy Event branch performs the state change with an unconditional transaction array and no status re-check on `registration`/`qrToken`. Two concurrent scanners (or a retry racing the first request) can both pass the preflight `registration.checkedInAt` check and both commit: the `update` sets status/checkedInAt again, a second `checkIn` row is created, and a duplicate achievement is attempted (points protected only by the achievement idempotency key). Mirror the Activity path: use `updateMany({ where: { id, status: { in: ["REGISTERED", "ATTENDED"] }, checkedInAt: null } })` inside the transaction and bail out with `already_checked_in` when `count !== 1`.

The QR token is consumed unconditionally here (no `status: "ACTIVE"` guard), so a token that was revoked/expired/consumed between the read and the transaction is silently overwritten back to CONSUMED rather than detected. This also breaks the concurrency guard above — scope the consume to `status: "ACTIVE"` and handle the zero-count case.

`triggerActivityRewards` is fire-and-forget with `void` and no `.catch()`. Rejections become unhandled promise rejections (noisy in Node, and under strict runtimes can terminate the process), and a failure is invisible to both the caller and the audit log even though the response reports `checked_in`. Attach a rejection handler that records an audit-log/metadata failure, or await it and fold the status into the response.

`createAchievementRecord` throws on real DB errors (it returns `null` only for a missing table, see lib/server/achievement-badge.ts:292-297) and is awaited AFTER the check-in transaction has already committed (both in the Activity and legacy Event paths). A throw here aborts the handler after the side effects are persisted, so the caller receives a 500 for a check-in that actually succeeded and will likely retry — with no try/catch the response is not even a valid JSON contract for the client. Wrap it (or the surrounding block) so a reward/achievement failure is logged and does not mask the committed check-in.

project_summary:
# Project-Level Review Summary

### Top Issues

1. **`requireRoleAccess`/`requireAuthenticatedUser` is misused as an API route guard, and the `instanceof NextResponse` check is dead code everywhere.**
   These helpers signal denial via `redirect()` (which throws `NEXT_REDIRECT`) and never return a `NextResponse`, so the guard `if (auth instanceof NextResponse) return auth;` is always false. In route handlers this produces opaque 500s/HTML redirects instead of 401/403 JSON, and in some cases actively defeats the intended authorization. This appears in dozens of routes: `apps/passport-web/app/api/activities/[id]/route.ts`, `.../activities/route.ts`, `.../activity-submissions/route.ts`, `.../admin/achievements/route.ts`, `.../admin/users/[userId]/role/route.ts`, `.../activities/[id]/speakers/route.ts`, `.../project-milestones/route.ts`, `.../admin/dispatches/route.ts`, and many more. Fixing the auth primitive (or introducing a route-oriented `requireApiRole`) is the single highest-leverage change.

2. **Missing error handling on `req.json()` and Prisma calls across nearly every route.**
   Malformed/empty bodies throw `SyntaxError`, and DB failures reject, both surfacing as unhandled 500s that leak stack traces. This is the most frequently repeated comment in the corpus: e.g. `apps/passport-web/app/api/activities/route.ts`, `.../activity-tasks/route.ts`, `.../auth/login/route.ts`, `.../auth/register/route.ts`, `.../certificates/verify/[code]/route.ts`, `.../verifier/scan/route.ts`, `.../admin/institutions/route.ts`. Several routes also use `req.json().catch(() => ({}))`, which masks malformed JSON as a valid empty body (e.g. `.../admin/people/[id]/route.ts`, `.../admin/notifications/process/route.ts`).

3. **TOCTOU / check-then-act races instead of atomic guarded writes.**
   Read-then-create/update patterns that should be a conditional `updateMany`/`create` with constraint handling. Representative cases: `.../activity-checkin/route.ts` (self-check-in bypass), `.../activity-participations/[id]/route.ts` (status transition), `.../activity-submissions/[id]/review/route.ts` (double reward), `.../activity-applications/[id]/review/route.ts`, `.../activities/[id]/status/route.ts`, `.../activities/[id]/speakers/route.ts`, `.../activities/[id]/wishlist/route.ts`, `.../admin/institutions/route.ts` (slug), `.../admin/people/route.ts` (slug/userId).

4. **Privilege authorization gaps (IDOR / cross-tenant).**
   - Agenda items updated/deleted by `agendaId` without checking `activityId`: `apps/passport-web/app/api/activities/[id]/agenda/[agendaId]/route.ts`.
   - Reward/certificate rules not scoped to managed activity: `.../activity-reward-rules/route.ts`, `.../activity-certificate-rules/route.ts`.
   - Certificates/templates copy with role-only check, no tenant scoping: `apps/passport-web/app/api/admin/certificates/templates/[id]/copy/route.ts`.
   - Cross-issuer data exposure: `apps/passport-web/app/api/external/decision-receipts/route.ts`, `.../external/activity-taxonomy/withdraw/route.ts`.
   - Revoke/withdraw endpoints not scoping to the parent resource: `.../records/[id]/grants/[grantId]/route.ts`, `.../admin/achievements/[id]/revoke/route.ts`.
   - Writes that accept client-supplied `createdByUserId`/`managerUserId`/`userId` without deriving from the authenticated user: `.../activities/route.ts`.

5. **`"en" as any` locale casts (and hardcoded locale/paths) throughout API routes.**
   Bypasses the `Locale` type and forces English redirects, breaking non-English and hiding type errors. Seen in `.../activities/[id]/stats/route.ts`, `.../admin/users/[userId]/role/route.ts`, `.../activity-submissions/route.ts`, `.../admin/notifications/[id]/attempts/route.ts`, `.../activities/[id]/verifiers/route.ts`, `.../qr/identity/route.ts`, and many more. Sibling endpoints even diverge (some derive locale from the request, e.g. `me/portfolio/route.ts`).

6. **`as any` / `as never` bypasses on writes and query filters.**
   Prisma `where`/`data` payloads cast via `any` defeat enum/field checking and let invalid input reach the DB, producing runtime 500s rather than 400s: `.../activity-participations/route.ts` (status), `.../me/achievements/route.ts` (`as never`), `.../me/badges/route.ts` (`as never`), `.../activities/route.ts` (status/type), `.../activity-applications/export/route.ts` (`status as any`), `.../admin/certificate-applications/route.ts`.

7. **Audit-trail integrity failures.**
   Either audit writes are fire-and-forget with `.catch(() => undefined)` (silent gaps on privileged actions): `.../admin/institutions/route.ts`, `.../admin/people/route.ts`, `.../admin/speakers/[id]/person/route.ts`, `.../certificates/[id]/artifact/route.ts`, or they run outside the state-changing transaction: `.../admin/portfolio/rules/[id]/activate/route.ts`, `.../admin/certificates/[id]/revoke/route.ts`, `.../activities/[id]/people/route.ts`. Both patterns undermine compliance/audit guarantees.

8. **Error-dispatch via substring matching on internal error messages.**
   Status codes inferred from `message.includes("not found")` etc., coupling routes to another module's copy and misclassifying HTTP semantics: `.../admin/invitations/[id]/qr/route.ts`, `.../admin/invitations/[id]/qr/revoke/route.ts`, `.../admin/special-passes/[id]/qr/route.ts`, `.../admin/special-passes/[id]/qr/revoke/route.ts`. These also echo raw internal messages to clients.

9. **Hardcoded Host-derived URLs embedded into certificates/QRs.**
   `new URL(request.url).origin` feeds verification/QR URLs that are persisted, so a spoofed `Host`/`X-Forwarded-Host` yields poisoned verification links: `.../admin/certificates/issue/route.ts`, `.../admin/certificates/batches/[id]/process/route.ts`, `.../admin/certificates/templates/preview/route.ts`, `.../activity-certificate-rules/route.ts`. Should come from trusted config (`APP_URL`).

10. **Rate-limiter configuration defects.**
    Synchronous in-process `checkRateLimit` (per-instance, effectively global when proxy trust unset): `.../summer-school/application-lookup/route.ts`, `.../summer-school/passport-id/route.ts`. Missing `sensitive: true`: `.../certificates/verify/[code]/route.ts`, `.../verify/badge/[token]/route.ts`. Rate limit before auth with shared bucket: `.../qr/identity/route.ts`, `.../verifier/scan/route.ts`, `.../channel/session/bridge/route.ts`.

### Module Hotspots

- **`apps/passport-web/app/api/activities/**`** — by far the densest: agenda, applications, community, detail, leaderboard, stats, speakers, institutions, status, wishlist, submissions, tasks, occurrences, checkin, people, classifications. Dominated by authorization gaps, TOCTOU races, `any` casts, and missing try/catch.
- **`apps/passport-web/app/api/admin/certificates/**`** — certificates, batches, categories, templates, rules, issue: Host-header injection, non-atomic writes, misclassified status codes, orphaned artifacts on partial failure.
- **`apps/passport-web/app/api/admin/institutions/**`** — governance, merge, representations, [id]: cycle creation, tenant scoping omissions, empty-update audit noise, swallowed audits.
- **`apps/passport-web/app/api/admin/external-learning/**`** — accounts, providers, course-mappings, evidence, inbox: audit action-name bugs, `403 UNAUTHENTICATED` semantics, bare-catch → 409, secret exposure in GET.
- **`apps/passport-web/app/api/auth/**`** — login, register, forgot-password, reset-password, verify-email, session: enumeration leaks, orphaned tokens, partial-success contracts, cache headers.
- **`apps/passport-web/app/api/channel/**` and `apps/passport-web/app/api/v1/channel/**`** — SHCW constant drift, fail-open auth bypass, cache headers on session responses.
- **`apps/passport-web/app/api/admin/{badge-definitions,achievements,badge-awards,special-passes,dispatches,notifications,portfolio}/**`** — largely a repetition of the auth-guard and error-handling issues.

### Cross-Cutting Concerns

- **Unsafe `any`/casts:** `"en" as any`, `status as any`, `as never`, `as unknown as Record<string, unknown>` appear in dozens of files (e.g. `.../activities/[id]/route.ts`, `.../me/badges/route.ts`, `.../institutions/[id]/route.ts`, `.../people/[id]/claim/route.ts`) — violates the stated no-`any` rule.
- **Pagination fragility:** `parseInt` → `NaN` propagating into `skip`/`take` in `.../activities/route.ts`, `.../activity-checkin/route.ts`, `.../activity-submissions/route.ts`, `.../activity-participations/route.ts`, `.../leaderboard/route.ts`. Unbounded `findMany` with no `take` in `.../summer-school/applications/route.ts`, `.../learning-experiences/programs/route.ts`, `.../admin/institutions/[id]/route.ts`.
- **Response cache-header inconsistency:** PII/token responses missing `Cache-Control: no-store` — `.../auth/session/route.ts`, `.../qr/identity/route.ts`, `.../public/portfolio/[token]/route.ts`, `.../me/portfolio/export/route.ts`, `.../assets/[id]/route.ts`, `.../admin/summer-school/applications/route.ts`, `.../v1/channel/session/exchange/route.ts`.
- **Duplicated prelude:** most `admin/**` and `activities/**` handlers repeat the same auth+role+Prisma+503 prologue; extraction would eliminate the recurring `instanceof NextResponse` dead-code pattern (e.g. `.../activity-tasks/[id]/route.ts`, `.../project-milestones/route.ts`, `.../activity-reviews/route.ts`).
- **Validation ordering inverted:** authorization/DB checks performed before body/auth validation, causing existence oracles and wasted work — `.../admin/institutions/representations/[id]/revoke/route.ts`, `.../admin/people/[id]/affiliations/route.ts`, `.../activity-tasks/route.ts`.
- **PII/secret over-fetch:** whole Prisma rows serialized instead of explicit `select` — `.../admin/summer-school/applications/route.ts`, `.../me/portfolio/share-links/route.ts` (`tokenHash`, `userId`), `.../admin/external-learning/providers/route.ts` (`signingSecretRef`), `.../dashboard/profile/route.ts` (`passCode`), `.../admin/dispatches/route.ts` (`lastError`, `receiptJson`).

### Quick Wins

1. **Replace `req.json()` with a guarded parse** in a shared helper (and stop collapsing failures to `{}`), then apply across `api/**`. Eliminates the most common 500 source.
2. **Audit-pass on `auth instanceof NextResponse`:** either introduce a route-oriented auth helper or delete the dead branch to expose real failures instead of masking them.
3. **Replace every `"en" as any` with a typed `Locale` value**, and derive the request locale where redirects matter. Machine-applyable across the ~20+ occurrences.
4. **Bulk-add `Cache-Control: no-store`** to session/token/PII/QR responses (`auth/session`, `qr/identity`, `public/portfolio/[token]`, `me/portfolio/export`, `assets/[id]`).
5. **Fix `parseInt` → `NaN`** by routing pagination through a small `clampInt(v, default, min, max)` helper across `activities`, `activity-checkin`, `activity-submissions`, `activity-participations`, `leaderboard`.
6. **Derive `verificationUrlBase` from `APP_URL`** in `admin/certificates/**` and `activity-certificate-rules` — one config lookup removes an entire class of Host-header injection.
7. **Correct the audit action-name template literal** in `.../admin/external-learning/accounts/route.ts` (`..._VERIFYD`/`..._DISABLEDD`) and add `.catch(err => log(err))` at minimum to the fire-and-forget audit calls.
8. **Add `try/catch` around the `deleteMany`/`createMany` pair** in `activities/[id]/agenda/[agendaId]/route.ts` and wrap in a transaction — small change, prevents data loss.
9. **Standardize `401` for `UNAUTHENTICATED`** replies (currently `403` in `admin/external-learning/*`, `v1/channel/*`) so clients can distinguish login vs. permission.
10. **Add a shared `requireApiRole`/`withRouteAuth` wrapper** so the extremely duplicated auth+Prisma+error-handling boilerplate collapses to one place.
